import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Recurrence for Rule 167 cellular automaton sequence

Decimal representation of the middle column of the "Rule 167" elementary cellular automaton
starting with a single ON (black) cell.

*References:*
- [A267581](https://oeis.org/A267581)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA267581


open Nat Int

/-- The rule function for Rule 167. Inputs must be 0 or 1. -/
def caRule167 (c_L c_C c_R : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let R : ℕ := 167
  let index : ℕ := 4 * c_L + 2 * c_C + c_R
  -- Rule 167 is determined by the index-th bit of R.
  (R / (2 ^ index)) % 2

/--
The state of the Rule 167 elementary cellular automaton at time $t$ and position $x$.
The initial condition is a single ON cell at $x=0$.
$C(t, x)$ is structurally recursive on $t$.
-/
def caState (t : ℕ) (x : ℤ) : ℕ :=
  match t with
  | 0 => if x = 0 then 1 else 0
  | t' + 1 =>
    let C_t' (y : ℤ) := caState t' y
    caRule167 (C_t' (x - 1)) (C_t' x) (C_t' (x + 1))

/-- The sequence of bits forming the middle column of the CA pattern, $C_{t, 0}$. -/
def middleColumnBit (t : ℕ) : ℕ := caState t 0

/--
Decimal representation of the middle column of the "Rule 167" elementary cellular automaton
starting with a single ON (black) cell.
The term $a(n)$ is the decimal value of the binary number $C_{0, 0} C_{1, 0} \dots C_{n, 0}$,
where $C_{i, 0}$ is the state of the center cell at time $i$.
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n C_{k, 0} \cdot 2^{n-k}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.sum (Finset.range (n + 1)) fun k => (middleColumnBit k) * (2^ (n - k))

/-- The floor term in the conjectured recurrence relation for A267581.
This term, $\lfloor (1/2)^{(2^{n+1} \bmod n)} \rfloor$, simplifies to 1 if $(2^{n+1} \bmod n) = 0$
(i.e., $n \mid 2^{n+1}$), and 0 otherwise.
Since the recurrence is only stated for $n \ge 2$, the $n=0$ case is irrelevant
to the conjecture. -/
def oeisFloorTerm (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0
  else if (2 ^ (n + 1)) % n = 0 then 1 else 0


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 3 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 6 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 13 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 26 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n) = 2 a(n-1) + 1 - \lfloor (1/2)^{2^{n+1} \bmod n} \rfloor$ for $n \ge 2$. - _Andres Cicuttin_, Mar 29 2016

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/267581.wip.lean#L190"]
theorem a_recurrence (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : a n = 2 * a (n - 1) + 1 - oeisFloorTerm n := by
    sorry

end OeisA267581

reformulations.difference: Replaces the source's real-valued floor expression by the natural-number indicator oeisFloorTerm, and states the recurrence using natural-number subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 2, put r = 2^(n+1) % n. If r = 0, then floor((1/2)^r) = 1; otherwise 0 < (1/2)^r < 1 and its floor is 0. Thus oeisFloorTerm is exactly the source's floor term. Moreover, oeisFloorTerm n ≤ 1 ≤ 2*a(n-1)+1, so natural subtraction never truncates. /workspace/review/equivalence.lean proves the universally quantified Lean statement equivalent to the literal-floor equality over ℤ, without using a_recurrence or any sorry-dependent result.

sources_consulted: OEIS A267581, complete entry via the official OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A267/A267581.seq (revision 32, August 19, 2026).

George Tsoukalas et al., Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search, arXiv:2605.22763v2, §3, OEIS paragraph. Abstract: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.22763v2.

Tom Adamczewski, OEIS Open: How many conjectures can language models turn into theorems?, arXiv:2608.11941, Appendix A.1, A267581 table entry and proof summary. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2608.11941.
review.notes: Checked all five definitions, five test lemmas, and the recurrence. Lean evaluations verified the complete Rule 167 truth table and a(0) through a(11). Kernel-checked auxiliary proofs establish that every caState value is a bit and that a(n+1) appends the next central bit. An independent finite-cone simulation matched all 1,001 OEIS b-file terms and the recurrence for n=2..1000. The excluded cases n=0 and n=1 fail, confirming the importance of the lower bound. The solved tag agrees with OEIS's May 28, 2026 proof announcement. After compatibility edits confined to the sandbox, the OEIS-linked AlphaProof Nexus proof compiled and was transferred to this file's exact statement; its axiom list contains only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound (/workspace/review/source-proof-check.lean). Direct OEIS HTML was blocked, so the complete entry was read through its official data mirror. The reviewed file is unchanged.
